Architecture discussion

This thread asks how a web reader can distinguish a deliberate bounded response from a source that was silently cut off. The first page is internally coherent and long enough to look trustworthy. That is exactly why pagination must be independent verifier evidence rather than a cosmetic outline flag.

Opening post

The author proposes a value axis for core versus full coverage. A core read is requested explicitly, names what remains, and reports the cost of retrieving it. Completeness answers a different question: whether the attempted source capture silently missed material. The two answers can coexist without changing one another.

Replies on page one

Several replies agree that an ordinary fetch of page one is not a deliberate core read. The caller asked for the thread and the generic reader stopped at a next-page link. Until a site recipe follows pages two and three and validates their manifests, the honest verdict is incomplete. Rendering page one again cannot solve that gap.
